nodes.description: Root node representing the individual receiving therapy.
Records of patient’s history, presenting complaints, and relevant contextual information.
Individualized models: hypotheses about maintaining processes, target thoughts, assumptions, and their evolution.
Key automatic thoughts, core beliefs, conditional assumptions, and higher-order schemas including metacognitive beliefs.
History of completed behavioral experiments: predictions, actions taken, outcomes, and reflections/learning.
Catalogue of safety and avoidance behaviors, their frequency, context, and changes over time.
Patterns and evolution of primary and secondary emotional, behavioral, and physiological responses to events and interventions.
Progression of collaboration, rapport, boundary management, and interpersonal schema testing within therapy.
Longitudinal cognitive, affective, behavioral changes, skill acquisition, degree of belief change, and generalization into everyday life.
Encountered barriers, triggers, implementation issues, disclosure difficulties or shame.
Mental and physical health disorders existing alongside presenting problem, including symptom changes and their interrelations.
Trusted companions, family relationships, resources, and supportive interpersonal/social connections.
Relevant background including physical health risks, medical investigations, disabilities, and medication adherence.
Patient’s functioning in social, occupational, academic, and daily living domains.
Sociocultural, developmental, language-based, and contextual influences on cognition, engagement, and expectations.
History of formative experiences, losses, trauma (including abuse, neglect, bullying), and associated memories and appraisals.
Depression, emotional numbness, PTSD, OCD, bipolar, phobias, social anxiety, and related symptom trajectories.
Patient’s self-esteem, shame, defectiveness, self-appraisal, and evolving sense of identity.
Catalog of adaptive and maladaptive coping strategies, help-seeking/assertion, and rescue/avoidance approaches.
Relapse history, management plans, early warning signals, prevention strategies, and vulnerabilities.
Patterns and styles of interpersonal behavior across relationships and contexts (e.g., assertiveness, withdrawal, hostility).
Functions, history, frequency, and progression of self-injury and associated facilitating beliefs.
Unique cognitive themes, maintaining factors, and relevant social context.
Latency, duration, quality of sleep, maladaptive sleep-related beliefs and behaviors, and impact on functioning.
Types/history of disordered eating, compensatory behaviors, beliefs about food/weight/shape/control, perfectionism, and motivation to change.
History/nature of illness or injury, adaptations, identity shift, and coping in and out of therapy.
Records of brain injury trajectory, assessments, feedback from external professionals, and social/occupational functioning.
Patient’s responses and reflections on diverse cognitive interventions across sessions.
